P-002: Include government hospitals among the approved Mbarara pilot providers.
P-005: P001 and GP0001 establish the project and group-batch formats, and each client or partner visit barcode also includes the security code. The format, allowed characters, lengths and uniqueness scope of every code, including batch, voucher and security codes, are still to be decided by the client.
P-006: Each group-batch always has 100 batches and each batch exactly 10 vouchers, and an authorized user may configure the minimum number of vouchers per creation run. The minimum number itself is still to be decided by the client.
P-007: Validity starts on creation, expiry blocks sales, treatment and claim acceptance, and a later date amendment affects sold vouchers. When validity ends is still to be decided by the client.
P-008: An authorized user may release a withheld voucher, and each blocked action is rejected rather than merely warned about. Which actions withholding blocks (distribution, retail sale, treatment, claim acceptance and/or payment) is still to be decided by the client.
P-010: Use a fixed approved retail price. The actual amount is recorded for each retail sale, and sales above the maximum retail price are rejected.
P-012: Limit returns to the returning distributor's unsold and unused vouchers. Accepted returns become saleable again, and refunds use the original invoiced wholesale rate.
P-013: Voucher prices, sales, returns, drug prices and claims use whole currency units, and rounding occurs per item. The currency and the rounding method are still to be decided by the client.
P-014: One initial consultation and at most two follow-ups are confirmed, separately for the client and the partner, and repeat or out-of-order visit claims are rejected. The permitted follow-up intervals and provider changes are still to be decided by the client.
P-015: Treat an out-of-network referral as a recorded destination and reason, without voucher reimbursement; at least the destination's name and location and the referral reason are required.
P-020: The HIV-details form, with its fields, allowed values and conditions for capture when HIV information exists, is still to be provided by the client; until then, no additional HIV-specific claim validation can be specified.
P-021: An unreadable print, an absent prior print or an unavailable reader puts the claim on hold. How the thumbprint on a paper claim is digitized and compared with prior prints, the exception approver, and the required evidence and audit record are still to be decided by the client.
P-022: Thumbprint mismatches share the more-than-two-event threshold, events are counted for all time, and an inactive provider can submit claims for treatments completed before inactivation. Which confirmed claim irregularities count as fraud is still to be decided by the client.
P-024: A deviating claim is accepted. The approved TA-OBA treatment matrix by syndrome and visit, the permitted deviations and the required justification are still to be supplied by the client.
P-025: The approved treatment matrix is authoritative when its amounts differ from the provider-term and drug-price formula. How the consultation, laboratory and drug components are calculated, and how discrepancies affect payment, are still to be decided by the client.
P-026: The first-visit laboratory fee is payable only if a test was actually performed, and several performed tests earn one contracted lab fee.
P-027: Adopt one reimbursable retail price per drug for all providers.
P-028: The treatment date is the effective date for provider fees and drug prices, effective periods may not overlap, and retrospective rate changes recalculate accepted claims.
P-029: Bi-monthly means twice per calendar month. The start and end of each submission and payment period and its cutoffs, for both bi-monthly and monthly providers, are still to be decided by the client.
P-030: The system only calculates claims and produces payment reports, and cash is allowed alongside bank transfer.
P-032: Each feedback record selects the client or the partner and one visit, treatment success comes from patient feedback, and partner-treated is derived from an accepted partner claim.
P-033: Counseling and privacy satisfaction use the treatment-satisfaction scale ('Not at all / Moderate / Good / Completely'), and each response concerns the client. The treatment-success response values are still to be decided by the client.
P-034: The Programme Design Study, and the data sources, numerators, denominators and classification rules for documentation quality, algorithm adherence, justified alterations and treatment errors, with the time periods and comparison method for their trends, are still to be supplied by the client.
P-036: The user groups and their create, edit, delete, view and print permissions for vouchers, validity, providers, payment terms, claims, payments and reports, and which groups may view or change client identity, HIV details and thumbprints, are still to be decided by the client.
P-037: Each type of sensitive detail (patient identity, HIV data and thumbprints) is masked in printed reports. The confidentiality and access restrictions, the required access and change audit logs, and the retention periods and disposal rules are still to be decided by the client.
P-038: The password-strength requirements, the failed-login threshold and lockout duration, the verified password-reset process and the idle-session timeout are still to be decided by the client.
P-039: Deletion is allowed. Which entered claims, distributions, retail sales, returns and payments each group may correct or cancel, including after finalization, is still to be decided by the client.
P-040: The measurable pilot and expansion targets for interactive response time, report generation, availability, concurrent users and daily and peak transaction volumes, distinguishing the 20,000-voucher pilot from later capacity, are still to be decided by the client.
